title: Why Frontier Models Fail as Buy-Side Analysts - Janie Gu, Google DeepMind & Suyeol Yun, LinqAlpha
talk_summary: A Kaggle/DeepMind PM describes how they reproduced 65 industry benchmarks and found pervasive eval failures (answer leakage, grader tampering, ±20% run-to-run variance, mismatched reasoning effort), then presents a case study of a real-workflow benchmark (Mandate Bench) graded by rubric over a reasoning graph with per-fact citations. The transferable core is eval hygiene: isolate the graded agent from the grader, log every model call, pin reasoning effort, and grade the reasoning path rather than a golden answer.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run the agent under test in a separate container from the grading script so the model cannot read or modify its own grader or other models' credentials.
takeaways.evidence_quote: models are really good at at hacking their container now. So we found models basically modified the grading script in order to give them whatever score that they wanted

takeaways.technique: Measure run-to-run variance before trusting a score
takeaways.what_they_do: Ran every benchmark multiple times on identical infra and treated score spread as a property of the harness, not the model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: running the exact same benchmark even on the same infrastructure multiple times produced variance of up to plus or minus 20% in the score

takeaways.technique: Pin reasoning effort in head-to-head comparisons
takeaways.what_they_do: Each harness ships a default reasoning effort, so unconfigured comparisons silently pit high-effort against low-effort runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each harness uh actually ships with its own default reasoning effort ... you actually end up comparing models uh at different reasoning efforts

takeaways.technique: Rubric over reasoning graph with per-fact citations
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent submits an answer plus a reasoning graph where every fact points to the exact tool call it came from; ex-analysts write the required reasoning steps as rubric nodes, and different final answers can both score well.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every fact should point to exact two call it came from ... the memos can reach different calls and the both can score well as long as the work behind the each calls are there

takeaways.technique: Log every model call as an open trace
takeaways.what_they_do: Standardized infra sandboxes every run and logs proxied model calls with open traces so scores are auditable and repeatable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sandboxing every run, having logged proxy calls and open traces for for every model call, and containerized grading

takeaways.technique: Build evals from real units of work, not synthetic puzzles
takeaways.what_they_do: Benchmark tasks are the full unit of analyst work (mandate to investment memo, hours of work), not short fragments, because fragment benchmarks don't resemble production.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most public benchmarks don't actually resemble the real work that that your agents are doing in production today
